title: Benedict XIII's cipher letters to Francesc Climent, 1399-1416, Arxiu Capitular de Barcelona (catalogue 334)

steps.what: HathiTrust record 100676638 (Puig 1920) tried in curl and the built-in browser: Cloudflare challenge, not solved. archive.org: no copy.

Butllari de Catalunya (Fundació Noguera 2016), IFC 2024 Benedicto XIII volume, Cuella's Bulario IV, Suárez Fernández's Castilian documents, zaguan 2023 paper grepped for cifra/xifra/criptog: no mention of the ACB cipher letters.

Baucells i Reig 1978 (ACB Cisma d'Occident catalogue, PDF from the ACB site): codices and parchments only; the paper part (1,532 pieces) was uncatalogued; archivist Mas's note that Puig took Schism papers home 1920-30 and many were not returned.
Google Books full-view copy of Puig 1920 found (id CuOlkxWnk-EC, Wisconsin). Book pages and PDF were CAPTCHA-walled, but the in-volume search endpoint and signed page-image URLs answered.

In-volume search for cifra/clave/descifr: p. 466 n. 2 says italics mark the deciphered phrases and Puig rebuilt the key 'a fuerza de paciencia' from lines Climent left on docs. 1063, 461, 463; preface p. 2: 'los diez u once escritos con desconocida clave' deciphered. Appendix index lists 14 'Carta cifrada' items, 1399-1416.
Appendix pages of every cipher item fetched and checked for gaps and for what Puig left unread (page-by-page check by a subagent).

Found that Puig p. 475 carries an uncaptioned, sideways photogravure of the last page of XXXV (22 June 1400, doc. 1068), clear Latin alternating with cipher runs, with Puig's text of the same passage beside it; fetched at the maximum 1826 x 2500 px, rotated and deskewed (0.7 deg), lines segmented.

Known-plaintext alignment of two runs against Puig's italics: line 1-2 'cum duce Burgundie' after a dotted-V sign for the King of Aragon, line 8 'et presertim scribe qu...'. Consistent values u = cb (3x), e = delta (4x), s = T (2x), m = t (2x), d = double cross (2x), c/i = o, b = T-bar; one clash.

Attempted a sign-level transcription of the long run (lines 8-16, about 450 letters of known plaintext) at 3-4x with contrast enhancement: delta/d-with-mark/o/a and joined strokes cannot be separated consistently at this resolution; 'quo modo se habet' did not align. Stopped; recorded as blocked (illegible).

gaps.item: Fr. Pedro de Vico to Guillem Carbonell, 4 Dec 1398: one cipher line of unknown key (Puig app. XIX, p. 461 n. 3)
gaps.detail: Not printed; the ACB original is not digitised.

gaps.item: Two keys of Climent in doc. 595 that Puig could not apply

gaps.detail: Rebuildable from the p. 475 facsimile against Puig's text, but Google's scan of the 1920 halftone is too coarse; needs a 600-dpi scan or a photograph of ACB doc. 1068.

gaps.item: P. Jafet to Climent 15 Sep 1400 (doc. 1043) and Comuel to Climent (doc. 661), cited by Puig but not printed

outcome.notes: Read by Puig y Puig in 1920; nothing deciphered here. Added here: Meister's second-hand ACB report identified with Puig's printed decipherments; the 14 cipher items listed; the p. 475 facsimile found and two runs aligned, which confirms Puig where tested and gives a dozen tentative sign values; the unread remainder listed.

prior.where: Puig y Puig, Pedro de Luna (Barcelona 1920), appendix: deciphered by Puig himself from Climent's partial glosses; not cited by Meister (1906, earlier), Galende 2013, or the cryptologic literature checked.

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the target with /goal from the archive-scan lead (catalogue 334), naming Puig y Puig 1920 as the outstanding check. No target-specific intervention.
